consent.consentTextSummary: Founder authorized public use of these responses as founder_statement, without publication of email, telephone or private data.

coreFounderClaims.claim: Canal Barra should not be reduced to IRC-only because CanalBarra.com held user photos, thoughts and messages for the channel's community.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The IRC-only description omits the website where people left photos, thoughts and messages for the channel community.

coreFounderClaims.claim: The #barra IRC channel was the live core of the ecosystem, comparable to a real-time timeline without algorithmic filtering.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The IRC channel was the flagship/live core; with cable internet, users increasingly stayed online in the channel.

coreFounderClaims.claim: CanalBarra.com maintained cadastros, rules, operator lists and user messaging, functioning as a web persistence layer.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The website maintained cadastros, made rules and operator lists explicit, and allowed message exchange among users.

coreFounderClaims.claim: CanalBarra.com was a safer place than the disputed IRC topic for official Canal Barra agenda information and also hosted best-cadastro voting.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: Because the #barra topic was disputed, the website was a safer official information surface for Canal Barra agenda and voting.

coreFounderClaims.claim: Physical gatherings strengthened belonging and encouraged more civil behavior in the IRC environment.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: IRContros, luaus, parties and physical meetings tightened bonds, created belonging and encouraged people to behave more civilly in IRC.

coreFounderClaims.claim: Canal Barra is best understood as a social ecosystem, including IRC, site, ICQ side contact, cadastros, social memory and physical encounters.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The founder describes Canal Barra as a social ecosystem rather than merely an IRC channel with a homepage.

coreFounderClaims.claim: The Xoom phase was manually updated by the webmaster; the CanalBarra.com domain phase became dynamic in cadastros, voting and messages.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The Xoom page was webmaster-updated; under the proper domain, cadastros, voting and messaging became dynamic.

coreFounderClaims.claim: The Xoom phase published profile cadastros and IRContro photos.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: Xoom content included profile cadastros and IRContro photos.

coreFounderClaims.claim: The proper-domain CanalBarra.com phase introduced user-editable cadastro and voting.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The CanalBarra.com domain phase allowed voting and user-editable cadastros.

coreFounderClaims.claim: User profiles perpetuated IRC presence beyond the channel and recorded at least some events.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: Profiles preserved user presence beyond IRC and helped record events, though not all events were captured.

coreFounderClaims.claim: CanalBarra.com helped distinguish events originating from administration from unrelated attempts to use the IRC topic for promotion.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The website helped identify administrator-originated events and gave users confidence that other channel users would be present.

coreFounderClaims.claim: CanalBarra.com functioned as a portal for the social life of many IRC users, including programming and sometimes VIP-list coordination through the channel.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The website was viewed as a portal for the social life of IRC users; someone looking for something to do in Barra could check the site programming and coordinate via the channel.

coreFounderClaims.claim: Lucas_Rio implemented the ColdFusion and Microsoft Access structure, after which BarMan performed maintenance and improvements.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: Lucas_Rio implemented ColdFusion with Access; BarMan then maintained and improved the site.

coreFounderClaims.claim: The installation/configuration of ColdFusion and Microsoft Access made the site more scalable and growth accelerated after that change.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The site became more scalable and growth began to accelerate after the technical change.

coreFounderClaims.claim: The Los Angeles work/development experience contributed to the knowledge used in the dynamic web phase.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The Los Angeles experience helped teach scalable websites.

coreFounderClaims.claim: Founder, Master and Operator roles existed as access tiers, but OP meetings introduced justification, argumentation and review based on what was good for the channel.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: Founder could appoint Masters and Operators; Masters could appoint Operators; Operators could voice users. Access choices could be discussed and justified in OP meetings.

coreFounderClaims.claim: The June 1999 operator meeting is important because it shows Canal Barra had become institution-like, with non-unilateral decisions and access levels treated also as rights to argue and opine.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The June 1999 OP meeting indicates that decisions were not simply unilateral and that access levels were connected to voice in governance.

coreFounderClaims.claim: Other channels may have had similar elements, and the founder would welcome more well-preserved channels for comparison.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: Other channels could have had similar elements; more preserved channels would help comparison rather than necessarily weaken the case.

coreFounderClaims.claim: The pre-2001 period depends more heavily on founder memory, while Wayback captures help reconstruct later phases.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: The founder states that the pre-2001 period depends too much on his personal memory, while Wayback helps reconstruct later phases.

coreFounderClaims.claim: The repository should preserve nicknames as public historical identities while keeping hostnames, birth dates, civil names and emails private.
coreFounderClaims.responseSummary: Nicknames are treated as public identities; hostnames, birth dates, civil names and emails should remain private.

negativeOrLimitingClaims.responseSummary: It was a pre-platform social community with IRC, site, cadastros, photos, events, reputation and in-person gatherings.

summaryForUseInThesis: BarMan's founder statement supports the repository's anti-IRC-only framing while explicitly limiting overclaims. He describes #barra as the live core, CanalBarra.com as the web-backed persistence and official-information layer, and physical gatherings as belonging and reputation reinforcement. He identifies a manual Xoom phase and a later dynamic CanalBarra.com phase with cadastros, voting and messages, linked to Lucas_Rio's ColdFusion/Microsoft Access implementation. He also states what Canal Barra was not: not a modern Facebook-style feed, not an automated friendship graph, not a replacement for IRC, not an automatic ChanServ controller and not a profitable commercial platform. The statement also acknowledges survival-bias and memory limitations, especially for the pre-2001 period.
methodologicalNote: This record is a sanitized public metadata extraction from a private Google Forms CSV. The founder email and raw CSV are not published. This record must be used as founder_statement only, not as independent external evidence. Claims requiring archival, dataset or participant confirmation are explicitly marked as pending. The alleged second-half-2003 founder withdrawal is not confirmed in this form and should not be cited from this record.
